title: Share of people using the internet: World, North America, South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, 2005–2023

sources.title: World Development Indicators: Individuals using the Internet (% of population) (IT.NET.USER.ZS)
sources.note: 由 World Bank API（api.worldbank.org/v2，country=WLD;NAC;SAS;SSF，lastupdated 2026-10-08）取得；原始提供者 ITU。地區彙總值從 2005 年才有資料（2000–2004 為空），所以圖表從 2005 年開始

facts.text: The World Bank counts as internet users all people who went online at least once in the last three months, from any place and on any device, such as a computer, mobile phone or game machine.
In 2005, 15.6% of the world's people used the internet; by 2023 the share was 69.2%.
69.2% is more than two out of every three people (derived from the 2023 world value).
North America: 68.3% of people used the internet in 2005 and 93.3% in 2023.
South Asia: 2.1% in 2005, 14.7% in 2015, and 58.3% in 2023; the share rose fastest after 2015.
Sub-Saharan Africa: 2.0% in 2005 and 32.3% in 2023, so about two out of three people there (67.7%) were not online in 2023 (derived).
SDG 9 target 9.c calls for greatly increasing access to information and communication technology and for universal, affordable internet access in the least developed countries.
